question:
**Case Study: Business Inventory Management Using Matrices**

A company sells three products: P, Q, and R. The monthly sales (in units) for these products in January and February are represented by the matrices:

$J = \begin{bmatrix} 120 & 150 & 100 \\ 180 & 130 & 170 \\ 140 & 160 & 110 \end{bmatrix}$ and $F = \begin{bmatrix} 100 & 140 & 90 \\ 170 & 120 & 160 \\ 130 & 150 & 100 \end{bmatrix}$

where rows correspond to Branches A, B, and C and columns correspond to Products P, Q, and R respectively.

(a) Compute and interpret the matrix $S = J + F$.

(b) If the cost per unit for products P, Q, and R are $\begin{bmatrix} 200 \\ 250 \\ 150 \end{bmatrix}$, calculate the total cost matrix for each branch for January using matrix multiplication.

(c) If the goal for next month is to increase each branch's total sales by 10% over January, suggest a matrix operation to represent this scenario, and compute the projected sales matrix for next month.
explanation:
(a)

To find $S = J + F$:

$S = \begin{bmatrix} 120 & 150 & 100 \\ 180 & 130 & 170 \\ 140 & 160 & 110 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 100 & 140 & 90 \\ 170 & 120 & 160 \\ 130 & 150 & 100 \end{bmatrix}$

$= \begin{bmatrix} 220 & 290 & 190 \\ 350 & 250 & 330 \\ 270 & 310 & 210 \end{bmatrix}$.

Interpretation: The matrix $S$ gives the cumulative sales for each branch for Jan and Feb for each product.

(b)

Cost per unit vector: $C = \begin{bmatrix} 200 \\ 250 \\ 150 \end{bmatrix}$.

Total cost for January per branch: $J \times C =$.

$\begin{bmatrix}120 & 150 & 100 \\ 180 & 130 & 170 \\ 140 & 160 & 110\end{bmatrix} \times \begin{bmatrix}200 \\ 250 \\ 150\end{bmatrix}$.

Row 1: $120\times200 + 150\times250 + 100\times150 = 24000 + 37500 + 15000 = 76500$.

Row 2: $180\times200 + 130\times250 + 170\times150 = 36000 + 32500 + 25500 = 94000$.

Row 3: $140\times200 + 160\times250 + 110\times150 = 28000 + 40000 + 16500 = 84500$.

Total cost matrix: $\begin{bmatrix} 76500 \\ 94000 \\ 84500 \end{bmatrix}$.

(c)

To increase each entry of $J$ by 10%, multiply $J$ by 1.10.

Projected sales = $1.10 \times J$.

$= \begin{bmatrix} 132 & 165 & 110 \\ 198 & 143 & 187 \\ 154 & 176 & 121 \end{bmatrix}$.

Thus, the projected sales matrix increases every value by 10% over January sales.
